tweet_summary: User shares a personal anecdote: his neighbor bought a Cybertruck this week because Tesla is 'gonna stop selling Autopilot' and he wanted to avoid the subscription.
why_note_decision: This is a low-engagement (1750 likes) personal anecdote/observation, not a news claim. The tweet loosely conflates 'Autopilot' with 'FSD'; what Tesla actually ended Feb 14, 2026 is the one-time FSD purchase (Autopilot is becoming subscription-coupled too — Autosteer moved into FSD per Autobody News). The neighbor's behavior — buying before the subscription cutover — is consistent with reality even if the user said Autopilot instead of FSD. Note-not-needed; this is the wrong kind of pedantic correction for a casual personal anecdote, and the neighbor's underlying strategy isn't actually wrong.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is a casual anecdote and the conflation of 'Autopilot' with 'FSD' is loose-language, not a misleading factual claim — Tesla did end one-time FSD purchases Feb 14, 2026, and is also restructuring Autopilot so this matches the spirit of the anecdote. FAIL any note that drily corrects 'Autopilot → FSD' on a personal-anecdote tweet; that's exactly the pedantry raters rejected. If the bot writes anything, it should at minimum NOT contradict the basic premise that buying before Feb 14 secured a one-time license.

original_unhelpful_note.text: Tesla ended one-time Full Self-Driving (FSD) purchases Feb 14, 2026, not Autopilot. Buying after that date requires $99/month subscription, so the "just in time" claim to avoid fees is false. https://www.businessinsider.com/tesla-pulls-plug-on-one-time-purchases-of-fsd-2026-2
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Pedantic Autopilot/FSD swap on a casual anecdote; the 'just in time' framing isn't actually false — buying before Feb 14 did lock in one-time FSD.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Spirit of tweet is correct; Autopilot/FSD terminology is loose but the cutover and purchase strategy are real
fact_check.notes: Tesla ended one-time FSD purchase Feb 14, 2026 at $8,000; subscription is $99/mo. Tesla also restructured standard Autopilot, moving Autosteer into FSD. The tweet's gist (subscription cutover) is accurate.

importance.lens_rationale: Personal-anecdote tweet; not a misinfo concern.
